name: search_investigations
description: List the 24 PSI combustion investigations as cards; filter by fire-safety pillar, fuel phase, flight/ground or platform_kind, and rank by a keyword query. Each card has `location`: kind, vehicle, module, facility (CIR, MSG, MDCA, ...), crewed, expedition, uses_data_from (the flight investigations a ground or computation study reanalysed), also (e.g. drop-tower precursor tests), label and source quotes. Use it to say where a result comes from and to count investigations by setting. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

platform_kind.description: where the tests ran: iss (a rack or glovebox on the ISS), cygnus_free_flight (Saffire, in an uncrewed Cygnus cargo module after it left the ISS), drop_tower, ground_lab, computation

name: get_investigation
description: Full knowledge record of one investigation: question, physics (with equations), method, test matrix, measurements, PSI data, findings with quoted sources, fire-safety relevance, limitations, open questions; `publications` (the record's papers in order, each with a `review`: access, read_url, classification, summary, quoted items; an AI reading of the paper, null when not reviewed) and `publication_review` (counts by access and classification). `location` says where it ran (see search_investigations) and adds `facility_notes`: one plain sentence per facility or vehicle name, for explaining CIR, MSG, Cygnus and the like to a beginner. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

name: filter_tests
description: Rows of the per-test table (2,177 rows, of which 2,059 are single tests: fuel, O2, pressure, flow, outcomes, platform_kind). Use for any question about what was tested and what happened. To get one test, pass accession and test_id. For the lowest or highest, pass sort_by and a small limit (sort_by="x_o2_ambient", limit=3 gives the three lowest-oxygen rows). Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

fuel.description: a normalised fuel name, matched as a whole word: pmma, heptane (also n-heptane blends); ethane does not return methane. Names in the table: arizona road dust, butane, dibutyl phthalate, ethane, ethanol, ethylene, farnesane, hydrogen, hydrogen/methane, isooctane, japan wax, kapton, lampwick, methane, methanol, n-decane, n-dodecane, n-dodecane/isododecane, n-heptane, n-heptane/isooctane, n-octane, nomex, paraffin wax, pmma, pmma/nomex, propane, propane/ethylene, propanol/glycerol, propylene, pyrell, sibal fabric, silicone, teflon, ultem. An everyday name (cotton, candle, acrylic, cloth, ...) that matches none is read as the table's name and a note says so

config.description: substring: normal, inverse, coflow, droplet, opposed flow, concurrent flow

x_o2.description: ambient O2 mole fraction [min, max], between 0 and 1 (30% O2 is 0.30, not 30; a bound above 1 is refused)

pressure_kpa.description: [min, max]; null leaves that end open

flow_cm_s.description: [min, max]; null leaves that end open

outcome.description: solid-fuel runs of BASS (PSI-26) and BASS-II (PSI-25) only: how the flame ended, read from the crew's notes; each row quotes its source in outcome_quote and gives outcome_cause (blowoff, low_flow, nitrogen, unspecified) when extinguished. Null on most rows: not stated

outcome_action.description: extinguished runs of BASS and BASS-II: what was done to the flow when the flame went out. flow_reduced = it went out at a finite low setting (a quenching limit, the setting in outcome_setting when stated); flow_shut_off = the crew stopped the flow to end the run (not a limit); flow_raised = blowoff; none = it went out by itself at constant flow. Null when the words do not say. flow_cm_s on these rows is the log's single air-display value, not the flow at extinction

sheet_out.description: ACME gas flames (PSI-10 inverse flames of 2021-22, PSI-159) only: the ending ticked on the test's hand-filled sheet. ext_detect = the flame went out by itself; time_out = it lasted the scripted time; temp_limit = it was cut off because the burner got too hot (neither an extinction nor a full-length flame). An AI reading of a scan, not checked by a human

platform_kind.description: where the tests ran: iss (a rack or glovebox on the ISS), cygnus_free_flight (Saffire, in an uncrewed Cygnus cargo module after it left the ISS), drop_tower, ground_lab, computation; each row takes its investigation's location.kind (no PSI table row is a drop-tower test)

exclude_flags.description: drop rows carrying any of these flag codes

include_unrecorded.description: with x_o2, pressure_kpa or flow_cm_s: also keep the rows that have no recorded value in that column (default false leaves them out, and a note counts them by investigation)

test_id.description: one test id or several, as in the rows' test_id (spaces and case ignored); pass accession too, since ids repeat across investigations

sort_by.description: a column of the rows to order by before limit applies; a leading - sorts descending ("-burn_time_s"); rows without a value come last

sheets.description: attach to each PSI-10 / PSI-159 row its hand-filled ACME test sheet as `test_sheet`: ignited, hot or cool flame, how the flame ended (`out`), operator comments, file and page. An AI reading of a scan, not checked by a human: repeat that note

name: compare
description: Side-by-side comparison of investigations: question, fuels, tested ranges, sensors, key findings, limitations. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

name: coverage
description: Count tests on a 2-D grid (default ambient O2 against pressure) and report which reference atmospheres (ISS cabin, Moon habitat, exploration, spacesuit) have no data. Use for gap questions. A reference's `nearest_test` lists in `not_measured` the columns filled from the investigation's stated range, not measured for that test, and `fire_test` false when that test heated a sample to make smoke without burning it (`n_not_fire_tests_in_cell` counts those rows). Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

name: relevance
description: Rank investigations by relevance to a fire-safety scenario and state how far the nearest real test is from it. fuel_phase orders the ranking and does not filter it: investigations of that phase (`phase_match` true) come first, then the other phases, then the ones where nothing burned (`fire_test` false; not for pillar detection), each group by score, so a lower row can have a higher score; `nearest_test` is always a test of that phase (null if none), and `closest_same_phase_test` is the nearest one overall. Never present `nearest_test_other_phase` as a test of the requested material. A condition a test dict lists in `not_measured` was not recorded for that test: a value shown for it is the middle of the investigation's range in `condition_ranges` (stated range or assumed cabin air), so say so when quoting it. `closest_same_phase_test.setting` (and a `Setting` note) says where that test ran and how far a result from there carries to a real cabin: repeat it. A test dict with `fire_test` false (SAME, SAME-R: samples heated to make smoke) is not a burn: never present it as a fire test; `closest_same_phase_test` is always one where ignition was attempted, and its `result` says what the burn did (burn length 0 = no flame spread). Scenario names: iss-cabin, moon-habitat, mars-habitat, pressurised-rover, spacecraft-transit. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

scenario.description: scenario name, or {x_o2, pressure_kpa, flow_cm_s, gravity_g} with at least one of the first three: x_o2 a mole fraction (0.34, not 34), pressure in kPa, flow in cm/s, gravity in g. Other keys and impossible values are refused with an error that names the unit

name: find_evidence
description: Keyword search for passages: reviewed digest findings (with citation ids) and raw text of PSI documents (file and page; `transcribed` marks an AI model's reading of a scanned page). Keyword-based: use the documents' own terms and try synonyms. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

name: insights
description: Cross-investigation synthesis entries with citations. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

name: timeseries
description: Sensor time series of one test (decimated) with summary features (burn duration, peak temperatures, chamber pressure). Available for PSI-10, PSI-23, PSI-39, PSI-159 and Saffire-I/III (PSI-98, PSI-100). For 24 PSI-39 droplet tests the investigators' reduced data (droplet diameter, hot- and cool-flame diameter, radiometer power against time) are a second recording: test_point "FLEX-<test id>-reduced". Reads the raw NASA files: from disk in a local copy; the demo server fetches each from NASA PSI on first use and caches it, so a recording nobody opened before fails with 502 while PSI is down. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

name: predict
description: Small per-investigation statistical model. Without model_id: list models, their inputs, accuracy and valid domain. With model_id plus every input of that model as extra named arguments: prediction (none outside the fitted domain) and the nearest real tests. For a quantity: prediction and interval [low, high] in `unit`, interval_nominal (0.9, the target), interval_coverage (n_inside of n on held-out test days, per fuel under by.levels), interval_clipped and interval_low_unclipped (lower end cut at 0), interval_unclipped, interval_unavailable (why interval is null), prediction_below_floor (the estimate itself is below 0, so prediction and interval are null), prediction_unavailable (why prediction is null), prediction_raw (the estimate as computed, a diagnostic only), interval_method, accession (source). The full list is about 75 kB: pass compact=true to get only id, inputs with their valid domain, accuracy and what each model must not be used for. Models (id, investigation, use: question; inputs with their fitted range). A value outside a range, or in an untested gap, gives no prediction, only the nearest tests; a descriptive model never gives one. cfig_normal_self_extinction (PSI-159, descriptive): Once a normal (fuel-from-burner) spherical gas flame is lit, does it go out on its own (radiative self-extinction) before the scripted timeout? Inputs: x_o2_ambient 0.1797-0.3997, untested 0.25-0.35 (mole fraction); pressure_kpa 50.67-304 (kPa); fuel_flow_mg_s 0.125-3.215 (mg/s); fuel_fraction 0.031-1 (mole fraction (burner stream)); n_carbon 2-4 (C atoms (2 ethane, 3 propane, 4 n-butane); or set by fuel). cfig_inverse_self_extinction (PSI-159, predictive): Once an inverse (oxidiser-from-burner, fuel ambient) flame is lit, does it self-extinguish before the scripted timeout, and how strongly does chamber pressure matter? Inputs: pressure_kpa 49.54-331 (kPa (table values, ~9% above nominal fill)); x_o2_burner 0.15-0.85 (mole fraction (burner stream)); o2_flow_mg_s 1.342-9.084 (mg/s); n_carbon 2-4 (C atoms (2 ethane, 3 propane, 4 n-butane); or set by fuel). cfig_normal_ignition (PSI-159, descriptive): Does a normal flame light (hot ignition) for a given chamber O2, pressure and fuel stream? Inputs: x_o2_ambient 0.1797-0.3997 (mole fraction); pressure_kpa 50.67-304 (kPa); fuel_flow_mg_s 0.1-3.215 (mg/s); fuel_fraction 0.01827-1 (mole fraction (burner stream)); n_carbon 2-4 (C atoms; or set by fuel). cfig_inverse_ignition (PSI-159, descriptive): Does an inverse flame light, given the burner-stream O2 and chamber pressure? Inputs: x_o2_burner 0.12-0.85 (mole fraction (burner stream)); pressure_kpa 49.54-331 (kPa (table values)). flex_burning_rate (PSI-69, predictive): How fast does a free methanol or n-heptane droplet burn (d²-law constant K) in a given atmosphere? Inputs: is_heptane 0-1 (1 n-heptane, 0 methanol; or set by fuel); x_o2_ambient 0.12-0.34 (mole fraction); x_co2 0-0.7 (mole fraction; 0 if not given); x_he 0-0.45 (mole fraction; 0 if not given); pressure_kpa 70.17-309.3 (kPa); d0_mm 1.13-4.53 (mm). flex_methanol_extinction_diameter (PSI-69, predictive): At what droplet diameter does a burning methanol droplet go out? Inputs: d0_mm 1.61-4.35 (mm); x_o2_ambient 0.12-0.3 (mole fraction); x_co2 0-0.7 (mole fraction; 0 if not given); x_he 0-0.45 (mole fraction; 0 if not given); pressure_kpa 70.17-276.3 (kPa). cfi_reignition (PSI-39, descriptive): At 2-5 atm, does an n-dodecane (or n-/iso-dodecane blend) droplet re-ignite a hot flame from its cool flame after the first radiative extinction? Inputs: pressure_kpa 202.7-506.6 (kPa); d0_mm 3.872-6.433 (mm); iso_dodecane_fraction 0-0.4 (mole fraction of iso-dodecane in the fuel; or set by fuel; 0 if not given); x_he 0-0.59 (mole fraction; 0 if not given); x_o2_ambient 0.17-0.21 (mole fraction). spice_smoke_point_length (PSI-107, descriptive): How long is a microgravity co-flow jet flame at its smoke point, for a given nozzle and co-flow speed? Inputs: nozzle_mm 0.4064-1.6 (mm); flow_cm_s 9.125-57.08 (cm/s). Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

fuel.description: instead of the model's fuel input: n-heptane or methanol (is_heptane), ethane, propane or n-butane (n_carbon), n-dodecane (iso_dodecane_fraction 0)

compact.description: with no model_id: the short list (about 5 kB)

name: discrepancies
description: Errors and doubts in the original PSI experiment tables: conflicts with the raw sensor data (table value, raw value, evidence, action taken), every value this dataset changed, flag meanings and counts, statements resting on files PSI lists as removed, notes on errors in NASA's catalogue records (e.g. Saffire-I and III listed under the ISS flight program although they burned in Cygnus), and `source_disagreements`: a published paper by the investigators disagreeing with the PSI data (paper quote, read_url, locator, claim), shown but never applied to the tables; say it is the paper against PSI. Use whenever the user asks about data quality or when showing a test whose row has flags. The full list is about 90 kB: pass compact=true to list every entry with its identifying fields only, then call again with accession or test_id for the evidence. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

compact.description: every entry without evidence, quotes and claims (about 31 kB)

name: document_text
description: Our extracted text of one PSI file, so a scanned PDF without a text layer can be read and copied. Without page: the pages (locators: p1, p2 for PDFs; sheet, slide or all for other files) that have text. With page: that page's passages in order (text, locator, transcribed). transcribed=true is an AI model's reading of a scan; check it in the original. A file with no text returns no pages. Use when a user reads a document, or to quote a page that find_evidence pointed to. Each item of the result's `sources` has `url` (NASA PSI page, doi.org or our notes) and `label`: cite those.

file.description: file name as listed in sources or the PSI catalogue
